paper_metadata.title: Preparation and microstructure and properties of AlCuFeMnTiV lightweight high entropy alloy

evidence.section: abstract
evidence.quote: A new type of AlCuFeMnTiV lightweight high entropy alloy (LWHEA) was prepared by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS).

evidence.section: 3.2.3 Effect of sintering temperature on properties of alloy blocks
evidence.quote: The density of LWHEA blocks at different sintering temperatures was measured by the Archimedes method, and the hardness testing and the compression performance testing at room temperature were carried out. The test results are shown in Table 5.

evidence.section: 2. Materials and methods
evidence.quote: The QM-QX-20L omnidirectional planetary ball mill was adopted, the milling speed was set to 200 rpm, and the milling time was 0–36 h.

evidence.section: 2. Materials and methods
evidence.quote: Using the Φ12 mm high strength graphite mold, the sintering temperature was 950–1100 °C, the sintering pressure was 40 MPa, and the holding time was 10 min.

evidence.section: 3.1 Effect of ball milling time on alloy powder
evidence.quote: After further milling, the diffraction peaks of the BCC phase, which correspond to the (110), (200), and (211) crystallographic planes, appear, indicating that the alloying is complete and the single-phase solid solution of the BCC structure is formed after 36 h of milling.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Effect of sintering temperature on the microstructure of alloy blocks
evidence.quote: it can be determined that the gray matrix is the main phase of BCC.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Effect of sintering temperature on the microstructure of alloy blocks
evidence.quote: The dark gray area is rich in Fe and Ti, which is the B2 phase.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Effect of sintering temperature on the microstructure of alloy blocks
evidence.quote: Cu precipitates mainly at grain boundaries, forming a white FCC phase.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Effect of sintering temperature on the microstructure of alloy blocks
evidence.quote: The black part is the HCP phase rich in Al and Ti, which is not evenly distributed in the structure and is mainly distributed in point-like aggregation.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Effect of sintering temperature on the microstructure of alloy blocks
evidence.quote: Additionally, a large number of twins can be observed in the alloy structure, and the lamellar thickness of the twins is around 150 nm. It can be seen from Figs. 7 and 8 that the twins are the Cu-rich FCC phase.
